title: Compatibility with finite reduction
statement: In the six-functor datum of [def-sf-datum], let $f:X\to Y$ be a separated finite-type morphism, let $1\le m\le n$, and let $K\in D^b_{ctf}(X,A_{E,n})$ and $L\in D^b_{ctf}(Y,A_{E,n})$. Write $K_m=K\otimes^L_{A_{E,n}}A_{E,m}$ and $L_m=L\otimes^L_{A_{E,n}}A_{E,m}$ for their finite reductions. Then the square comparing $\operatorname{PF}_{f,K,L}$ and $\operatorname{PF}_{f,K_m,L_m}$ through the finite-reduction compatibilities of $Rf_!$, $-\otimes^L$ and $Lf^*$ commutes; hence $\operatorname{PF}_{f,K,L}$ is an isomorphism if and only if $\operatorname{PF}_{f,K_m,L_m}$ is.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sf-projection-factor-coordinates] to the given intrinsic finite-Tor constructible inputs and normalized tensor models. That lemma prepares the witnessed-flat-domain inputs via [lem-sf-pf-reduction-witnessed-flat-domains], applies [lem-sf-pf-reduction-proper-open-identities], and transports the two equations to these intrinsic coordinates. Thus both prescribed unit-realized children remain in the argument.

Paste the separate equations by the proved [lem-sf-projection-scalar-square]. Naturality of the proper coefficient comparison moves the open projection across it, the open equation substitutes the mixed tensor/pullback map, the proper equation moves it across the proper projection, and naturality of the reduced proper projection recombines the scalar mate. Unfold the three specified finite-reduction maps to obtain exactly the required commuting square.

Apply [lem-sf-finite-projection-presentation] at level n+1, which transports the known finite-ring projection invertibility to the supplied normalized intrinsic models. Quotient extension preserves the finite-Tor constructible domain by [thm-sf-ctf-stability]; identify the recorded quotient functor with this derived scalar extension by uniqueness of left adjoints. Apply the same single-level lemma at level m+1 to the reduced inputs. Each direction of the asserted equivalence returns the independently obtained invertibility proof.

blueprint_update.statement:
In the setting of [def-sf-datum], let $J\subseteq\Lambda$ be an ideal and let
$\rho$ be the reduction modulo $J$ of [lem-sf-reduction-compatibility]. Let
$c$ be a compactification of $f$ and let $\operatorname{PF}$ be the projection
transformation of [def-sf-pf] computed with $c$. For all
$K\in D(X_{\Et},\Lambda)$ and $L\in D(Y_{\Et},\Lambda)$:

1. the square

$$
\begin{array}{ccc}
\rho_Y\bigl(Rf^c_!K\otimes^L_\Lambda L\bigr)&\xrightarrow{\ \rho_Y(\operatorname{PF}_{f,K,L})\ }&
\rho_Y\,Rf^c_!\bigl(K\otimes^L_\Lambda Lf^*L\bigr)\\
\downarrow&&\downarrow\\
Rf^c_!K\otimes^L_\Lambda\rho_YL&\xrightarrow{\ \operatorname{PF}_{f,K,\rho_YL}\ }&
Rf^c_!\bigl(K\otimes^L_\Lambda Lf^*\rho_YL\bigr)\cong Rf^c_!\,\rho_X\bigl(K\otimes^L_\Lambda Lf^*L\bigr)
\end{array}
$$

commutes, where the left arrow is the associativity isomorphism, the right
arrow is the comparison of $Rf^c_!$ with $\rho$ of
[lem-sf-reduction-compatibility] (2), and the bottom right isomorphism is built
from the comparison of $Lf^*$ with $\rho$ of [lem-sf-reduction-compatibility]
(1) and associativity;
1. $\rho_Y(\operatorname{PF}_{f,K,L})$ is an isomorphism if and only if
$\operatorname{PF}_{f,K,\rho_YL}$ is;
1. the projection formula holds at $(K,L)$ if and only if it holds at
$(K,\rho_YL)$, and both hold.

proof.text:
(1) Put $N=(\Lambda/J)_Y$, so $\rho_Y=-\otimes^L_\Lambda N$, and the comparison of
$Rf^c_!$ with $\rho$ is the projection map at $(-,N)$ followed by
$Lf^*N\cong(\Lambda/J)_X$ [lem-sf-reduction-compatibility]. The square therefore
expresses the associativity of the projection map: tensoring
$\operatorname{PF}_{f,K,L}$ with $N$ and then applying the projection map at
$N$ agrees, through the associativity isomorphisms of $\otimes^L_\Lambda$ and the
monoidality of $Lf^*$, with the projection map at $L\otimes^L_\Lambda N$. By
[lemma-weil-pbc-projection-formula-compactified] the projection map of $c$ is
the composite of the proper-piece map of
[lemma-weil-pbc-projection-formula-proper-piece], which is the transpose of
$\varepsilon\otimes1$ through the monoidality of the pullback, with the
open-piece isomorphism of [lemma-weil-pbc-projection-formula-open-piece].
Both pieces are compatible with associativity: for the proper piece this comes
down to the counit–tensor description and the monoidality of the derived
pullbacks, and for the open piece to its construction from the unit of
$j_!\dashv j^*$. This is an identity of the specified morphisms, proved from
their constructions and not from agreement on stalks.

(2) In the square, the left arrow, the right arrow (by
[lem-sf-reduction-compatibility] (2), $\Lambda$ being finite) and the bottom
right isomorphism are isomorphisms. Hence the top arrow is an isomorphism if and
only if $\operatorname{PF}_{f,K,\rho_YL}$ is.

(3) Since $\Lambda$ is finite, the projection map of $c$ is an isomorphism at
every pair of arguments: the open-piece map is always an isomorphism
[lemma-weil-pbc-projection-formula-open-piece], and the proper-piece map is an
isomorphism by the proper projection formula with torsion coefficients
[lem-amb-proper-coproducts-projection]. So the projection formula holds at
$(K,L)$ and at $(K,\rho_YL)$.
